method: Paginated disease->phenotype association pull per MONDO id; regex-filtered object_label for thumb/1st-metacarpal/preaxial and radius terms. Executed from OpenScientist execute_code sandbox (cwd=/app, Python 3, requests). Sandbox has no write access to the job filesystem; results transcribed here via Write tool.
note_on_ids: First attempt used wrong MONDO ids (MONDO:0008113 TAR, MONDO:0007750 Holt-Oram) which returned sparse nodes (20 and 5 associations). Correct ids resolved via /search: TAR=MONDO:0010121, Holt-Oram=MONDO:0007732.

interpretation.confirms: FA (MONDO:0019391) is annotated in Monarch/HPO with exactly the radial-ray field elements the seed hypothesis names: radius (incl. Radial ray deficiency, Absent/Hypoplastic radius), 1st metacarpal (Aplasia/Short 1st metacarpal), and thumb (Absent/Short/Triphalangeal/duplication). FA spans BOTH reduction and duplication (preaxial polydactyly, thumb phalanx duplication).
interpretation.corrects_prior_finding: The structured HPO comparison does NOT support a clean 'TAR spares the thumb' discriminator: the TAR node also carries thumb annotations (Absent/Short/Broad/Adducted thumb). All three disorders share overlapping radius+thumb annotations. The clinical teaching that TAR obligately preserves thumbs concerns PENETRANCE/obligate presence, not absence of any thumb annotation; aggregated ontology annotations are noisier than the clean clinical rule.
interpretation.limitation: Monarch D->P associations are aggregate (multiple sources, not frequency-weighted, include child terms and variant/spectrum annotations). Counts (668 vs 115 vs 132) reflect curation depth, not phenotype prevalence. This is an ontology-annotation check, NOT mechanistic evidence and NOT a frequency analysis.
